sections.html:
McClain County lies in south central Oklahoma, just below Norman and Cleveland County, and Purcell is where the courthouse stands. The 2020 head count was 41,662 people living among 16,421 housing units. Roughly 79.8 percent of occupied homes belong to the people living in them, and 7.2 percent of units were empty. Think family houses, subdivisions and acreage rather than a rental-heavy market.

Blanchard, Newcastle and Purcell are the three cities. Byars, Cole, Dibble, Goldsby, Maysville, Rosedale, Washington and Wayne are towns. Three layers go into any McClain County bill: the county itself, the municipality, and the school district. Alex, Asher, Blanchard, Bridge Creek, Dibble, Lindsay, Maysville, Newcastle, Norman, Paoli, Purcell, Stratford, Washington and Wayne all run K-12 systems that levy separately. Drawing a district boundary between two equally priced houses can produce two different annual bills.

Interstate 35 carries most traffic, and drive time to the metro is typically the opening question from a prospective buyer.

Two courthouse offices share the job. One decides what each parcel is worth and compiles the roll. The other mails statements, accepts money and divides the receipts among the county, the cities and towns, and the schools. Both are in Purcell.

OfficeAddress and contactHours
Assessor121 N. 2nd Ave, Room 206, Purcell, OK 73080, 405-527-35208:00 to 4:30
Treasurer121 N. 2nd, Room 318, Purcell, 405-527-3261, treasurer@mcclaincountyok.gov8:00 to 4:30

If you would rather not drive, oktaxrolls.com has a searchable roll with payment. Beyond valuation, the assessor keeps land records and maps, accepts exemption paperwork, walks every property on a four-year inspection rotation and supports the board that fixes errors on the roll. Use the McClain County Assessor page and the treasurer page for up-to-date office information.

sections.h2: How a tax bill is built
sections.html:
Follow the money in order. Valuations pass from the assessor to the County Equalization Board and on to the State Board of Equalization. Next, the Excise Board certifies millage rates. The assessor then finalizes the roll and delivers it to the treasurer, who mails the statements. One mill is a dollar of tax for each $1,000 of taxable value. Assessment ratios in this state run 10 to 15 percent, and combined mill rates commonly fall between 90 and 110.

Since every taxing body picks its own levy, two neighborhoods rarely match. Read the school district printed on your bill instead of repeating a friend's number to a buyer.

  • Worth of the property: assessor, with a look at each parcel every fourth year.
  • Rates: the taxing bodies, certified by the Excise Board.
  • Statements: treasurer, after the roll is filed.

No first-half delinquency attaches until 30 days after the finished rolls reach the treasurer.

November 1 is when statements become payable. Paying in halves is allowed: one half ahead of January 1 and the other ahead of April 1. Miss that first half and everything is delinquent as of January 1.

  • Small balances, $25 or less, must be settled in a single payment before January 1.
  • Interest on overdue tax accumulates monthly at 1.5 percent, ending when it equals the unpaid amount.
  • Lenders that escrow taxes send one annual payment before the year turns.
  • The treasurer may forgive a penalty or interest if the lateness was not your doing.

Planning to close between November and March? Check with the treasurer whether half has been paid yet. An up-to-date account is simple, and an overdue one calls for a calculated payoff that the settlement agent will want sooner rather than later.

Send the assessor a written protest. Where the county mailed an increased-value notice, you have 30 calendar days from the postmark date. Where nothing changed, the deadline moves to the first Monday in April.

An informal hearing follows. The assessor must mail a written decision inside 7 calendar days. If the answer is no, 15 calendar days from the decision's mailing date remain to take the matter to the county board of equalization. The form wants valuation information attached, and leaving it off means the assessor's figure is presumed right.

Before filing, collect similar nearby sales, contractor bids for needed repairs and dated photos. Evidence earns a more serious hearing than frustration does.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and the 3 percent cap
sections.html:
If you live in the house, $1,000 comes off taxable value through the homestead exemption, and assessed value cannot rise more than 3 percent in a year for as long as you hold it. File with the assessor.

A sale starts the clock over. Whoever buys will see a first bill reflecting current value, which can top yours by a noticeable margin, so warn any buyer budgeting from your statement. The break travels with the occupant, so the buyer submits a new application after taking title.

Money owed on the parcel is deducted from what you receive at settlement. The settlement agent requests a figure from the treasurer. Weeds, cleanup, paving and nuisance abatement charged by a city become a lien on the parcel once delinquent and are certified to the treasurer, so ask whether any exist.

Land with years of unpaid tax eventually goes through the annual delinquent-tax sale, after which the treasurer manages it as county property. Behind on payments, or holding an inherited house with arrears? Find out the exact amount first.

  1. Look the parcel up at oktaxrolls.com and jot down each year carrying a balance.
  2. Call the treasurer for an interest-inclusive amount in writing.
  3. Ask city hall about certified mowing or cleanup bills.
  4. Hand the numbers to the settlement agent so your net proceeds are accurate.

Do the paperwork before a buyer asks for it. At the start, view the parcel record and see which years are open. Within a couple of weeks, ask the assessor whether a homestead filing or a correction is pending on the account. After a contract is signed, the settlement agent orders a payoff of its own, and any city lien shows up then. On the day of closing, the county is paid from your proceeds, so nothing follows the property to the buyer.

An all-cash buyer shortens the schedule because no appraiser or loan underwriter has to weigh in. Clear title is still required, so the tax and lien research is identical. Mention your school district early, since a buyer curious about taxes usually wants schools in the same breath.

The usual stories: someone inherited a house, repairs were postponed, a tenant lives in a rental, or taxes went unpaid. About one in five occupied homes in the county has a renter, so landlords are common.

A fast cash sale attracts owners who would rather skip open houses, inspection haggling and a lender's punch list. Condition differs around the county. Rural parcels near the Canadian and Washita rivers, hilly lots out west and older homes in Purcell and Byars each carry distinct repair questions, and an as-is sale hands those to the buyer. Whichever route you pick, get tax and lien amounts in writing first so your net is clear.

When you call anyone about the house, have these on hand: the parcel number, your latest statement, any valuation notice, deed or probate papers for an inherited property, and a plain list of problems you already know about.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my McClain County home?
faqs.a: The County Assessor sets it. The office is at 121 N. 2nd Ave, Room 206 in Purcell, phone 405-527-3520.

faqs.q: When does McClain County want property tax paid?
faqs.a: Statements are payable November 1. Half has to arrive before January 1 or the full levy goes delinquent, and the remaining half is due before April 1.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost?
faqs.a: Interest runs at 1.5 percent a month on overdue tax and stops growing once it equals the unpaid tax.

faqs.q: What is my deadline to dispute a value?
faqs.a: Thirty calendar days from the mailing date of an increase notice. If the value stayed put, file by the first Monday in April.

faqs.q: Will back taxes stop me from selling?
faqs.a: No. What you owe comes out of your proceeds at settlement, and the treasurer supplies the amount.
